newsitem.title: GERMANY: DEUTSCHE TAKES FULL CONTROL OF IVOR JONES.
newsitem.headline: DEUTSCHE TAKES FULL CONTROL OF IVOR JONES.

text.p: Germany's largest commercial bank, Deutsche Bank AG, said on Tuesday it was buying a further 50 percent stake in South African stockbroker firm Ivor Jones, Roy, giving it full control of the firm from January 1, 1997.
Deutsche took an initial 50 percent stake in the firm at the start of this year.
In a statement released in Frankfurt, Deutsche said IJR would in future operate under the name Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (Pty) Limited.
The brokerage, which employs 90 people in Johannesburg, Cape Town, London and New York, specialises in share and bond analysis.
Deutsche said the purchase was a further step in the globalisation of its investment bank unit Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
Deutsche already has two representative offices and a subsidiary in South Africa. Including IJR, it will have a total of 150 employees in the country.
